item.title: Sāriputta, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will have peaceful faculties, peaceful minds.' Sāriputta, you should train thus. For those with peaceful faculties, Sāriputta, and…
item.description:
Sāriputta, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will have peaceful faculties, peaceful minds.' Sāriputta, you should train thus. For those with peaceful faculties, Sāriputta, and peaceful minds, their bodily action will also be peaceful, verbal action peaceful, mental action peaceful. 'We will offer a peaceful gift to our fellow celibates.' Thus, Sāriputta, you should train yourselves.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.36

item.title: Dhāniya: No gadflies or mosquitoes are found here, The cattle roam on the grassy meadow, They can endure the rain when it comes. So if…
item.description:
Dhāniya:
No gadflies or mosquitoes are found here,
The cattle roam on the grassy meadow,
They can endure the rain when it comes.
So if you wish, O deva of rain, let it rain!

The Blessed One:
A raft is well made, firmly bound together,
Having crossed to the far shore, having overcome the flood,
There is no further need for a raft.
So if you wish, O deva of rain, let it rain!

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.2

item.title: Walking and standing with self-control, Sitting and lying down with self-control, The bhikkhu, self-controlled, When bending and stretching his limbs. Above, across, and all around,…
item.description:
Walking and standing with self-control,
Sitting and lying down with self-control,
The bhikkhu, self-controlled,
When bending and stretching his limbs.
Above, across, and all around,
As far as the end of the world,
Regarding whatever kind of existence,
In this world,
He well observes the arising and passing
Of all aggregates.
With mind peaceful, in right conduct,
Constantly training,
Continuously, diligently,
The bhikkhu is so called.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.12

item.title: Elder Paripuṇṇaka: Though one may enjoy food with a hundred flavors like nectar, It cannot compare with the meal I have today. This is the…
item.description:
Elder Paripuṇṇaka:

Though one may enjoy food with a hundred flavors like nectar,
It cannot compare with the meal I have today.
This is the wonderful Dhamma taught to me
By Gotama Buddha, the one of limitless vision.

From: Theragāthā 1.91

item.title: When the field is complete, The seed is sown complete, When the rain falls complete, The harvest is complete, When no calamity is present, Growth…
item.description:
When the field is complete,
The seed is sown complete,
When the rain falls complete,
The harvest is complete,
When no calamity is present,
Growth is complete,
Expansion is complete,
The result is complete.
So too, giving
Among those of complete virtue,
And the gift material
Is also completely obtained,
It leads to completeness
Because of complete conduct.
Therefore, whoever wishes completeness
Must themselves be complete,
Serving those of complete wisdom,
Thus success is complete.
Complete in wisdom and virtue,
With mind complete,
Doing deeds complete,
Benefit is complete.
Knowing the world as it really is,
One attains complete view.
The complete path leads to
Attaining complete intention.
Abandoning all defilements,
One attains complete Nibbāna.
Liberated from all suffering,
That is complete perfection.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.34

item.title: There are these two kinds of pleasure, bhikkhus. What two? Material pleasure and non-material pleasure. These, bhikkhus, are the two kinds of pleasure. The foremost…
item.description:
There are these two kinds of pleasure, bhikkhus. What two? Material pleasure and non-material pleasure. These, bhikkhus, are the two kinds of pleasure. The foremost among these two kinds of pleasure, bhikkhus, is non-material pleasure.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.68

item.title: These ten things, bhikkhus, are pure, bright, exist only in the Discipline of the Well-Gone One. What ten? Right view, right intention, right speech, right…
item.description:
These ten things, bhikkhus, are pure, bright, exist only in the Discipline of the Well-Gone One. What ten? Right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right knowledge, right liberation. These ten things, bhikkhus, are pure, bright, exist only in the Discipline of the Well-Gone One.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.123

item.title: Elder Kuṭivihāri (2): This hut is old. You want a new hut. Give up wanting a hut; a new hut brings new suffering. Know this,…
item.description:
Elder Kuṭivihāri (2):

This hut is old. You want a new hut.
Give up wanting a hut; a new hut brings new suffering.
Know this, O bhikkhu!

From: Theragāthā 1.57

item.title: Bhikkhus, what is the course of practice that is painful with slow direct knowledge? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the foul on the body,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, what is the course of practice that is painful with slow direct knowledge? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the foul on the body, with perception of disgust for food, with perception of non-delight in the entire world, contemplating impermanence in all formations, and the perception of death is well established internally. He lives depending on the five learner's powers, that is, the power of faith, the power of conscience, the power of fear of wrongdoing, the power of energy, the power of wisdom. For him, these five faculties appear very soft: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom. Because these five faculties appear very soft, he attains the immediate concentration for the destruction of the taints slowly. This, bhikkhus, is called the course of practice that is painful with slow direct knowledge.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.163

item.title: Brahmā, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the ancient teachers, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the devas of old, bhikkhus,…
item.description:
Brahmā, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the ancient teachers, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the devas of old, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; worthy of offerings and reverence, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, mother and father have done much for their children: they nourish them, bring them up, and introduce them to this world.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.62
